question: How many folds should cross-validation use under the current evaluation protocol?
answer: The current evaluation protocol uses k = 5 folds for cross-validation [S1] [S2] [S3].

citations.title: Ml Project Handbook
citations.text:
Evaluation Protocol v2
Evaluation protocol v2 supersedes protocol v1 for all projects started in 2025. Split the data 70% training, 15% validation and 15% test. Use k = 5 folds for cross-validation and report the mean and standard deviation of the fold scores. Set random_state=42 everywhere. The test set may be used exactly once. The primary metric is F1 for imbalanced data and accuracy otherwise.

citations.text:
Split the data 60% training, 20% validation and 20% test.
Use k = 10 folds for cross-validation.
The primary metric is accuracy.
Fix the random seed to 0.

citations.title: Ml Lecture Notes
citations.text: 5. Data Splitting and Cross-Validation Data is usually divided into a training set for fitting, a validation set for tuning hyperparameters and a test set used once for the final unbiased estimate. Using the test set repeatedly for decisions leaks information and makes the estimate optimistic. Data leakage more generally means that information from outside the training data, such as future values or the target itself, influences the features; it produces unrealistically good scores that collapse in production. k-fold cross-validation splits the training data into k equal folds. The model is trained k times, each time holding out a different fold for validation, and the k scores are averaged. Typical values are k = 5 or k = 10. Stratified k-fold preserves the class proportions in every fold and is recommended for classification with imbalanced classes.

S5.title: Ml Model Diagnostics Handbook
S5.text:
4. Class Imbalance and Validation Practice
For imbalanced classification set class_weight='balanced' so that rare classes receive a larger
weight in the loss, or resample the training folds. Oversampling must be done inside each training
fold only; oversampling before splitting leaks duplicated rows into the validation fold. Report the
precision-recall curve or F1 rather than accuracy.
A common validation setup is StratifiedKFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=True, random_state=42). The
helper cross_val_score(estimator, X, y, cv=5, scoring='f1') returns one score per fold. For time
series use TimeSeriesSplit so that the training data always come before the validation data.
